subject: NimbleWorks integration: bridge version harmonization & soft-deprecation plan
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@nimbleworks.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Gonzalez <sofia@nimbleworks.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge v1.x compatibility / deprecation ask

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Hope you're both well — quick note from the NimbleWorks platform team. We recently started a customer project that depends on your legacy Bridge v1.2 SDK (the HTTP blocking client). We see a note in the public changelog about the new async streaming API and a planned deprecation, and we need clarity on timing and migration support.

As a partner, our ask is: can Redwood commit to a soft-deprecation window and provide a compatibility matrix + test harness we can run against our CI? Specifically: 
- Target deprecation date (if any) for Bridge v1.x
- Any incompatibilities we should expect with the async streaming endpoints (tokenization differences, session semantics, error codes)
- Recommended migration path and whether you’ll provide a compatibility shim we can vendor-in

This matters because we have a set of enterprise customers who require a 3–6 month upgrade path and automated regression checks. Happy to join a technical sync next week. I attached our high-level request doc.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
Head of Integrations — NimbleWorks
[attachment: nimbleworks_compat_req.pdf]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@nimbleworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge v1.x compatibility / deprecation ask

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Putting a short proposal on the table so we have a working plan to discuss on a call: 

Mutual action plan (proposal)
- Week 0 (this week): Tech triage call to capture precise API surface your product uses (we can run the test harness against your integration).
- Week 1–4: Joint compatibility testing using our test runner + your CI; we’ll share a change matrix (attached).
- Week 5–12: If a shim is required, Redwood will prioritize a compatibility adapter (soft-shim) that sits on Bridge v1->async. Estimated engineering effort: 6–8 weeks.
- Soft-deprecation begins no earlier than 2027-03-01 with a 6-month window to GA cutover and public sunset.

We are willing to provide the test harness and a prebuilt shim as long as we get partner sign-off on the canary schedule. I attached the initial change matrix and a draft partner migration pack.

Can we set an hour next Tuesday 10:00 PDT for the triage? Ben — loop in infra if you need to. Lauren — I'll need the partner-facing kit ready if they sign off.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
[attachment: nimbleworks_sdk_change_matrix.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@nimbleworks.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge v1.x compatibility / deprecation ask

On Fri, Sep 4, 2026 at 11:05 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> We are willing to provide the test harness and a prebuilt shim as long as we get partner sign-off on the canary schedule.

Rajiv — quick technical notes from my side after a pass on v1.2: 
- Bridge v1 is blocking and assumes synchronous token emission; the new async streaming API returns chunked frames and different transient error codes.
- Most incompatibilities are wiring: session lifecycle, backpressure, and the framing of function/call metadata.
- We can deliver a shim that translates v1 semantics to the streaming API, but it will add ~10–12ms per request in worst-case path and needs coverage in your integration tests.

Suggested engineering plan (concise):
1) Build shim + feature-flagged adapter inside the Bridge library (6–8 weeks).
2) Provide a Dockerized test runner and a small set of smoke tests (2 weeks) that you can bake into your CI.
3) Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic (2 weeks) -> 25% (2 weeks) -> 100% (1 week) if no regressions.

For telemetry: we can expose a partner-only telemetry dashboard (token-level error rates, latency percentiles) during canary so your SREs can validate. I’ll need to coordinate with infra on retention.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@nimbleworks.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Partner migration pack + weekly sync cadence

Hi Rajiv — following up from the triage. Attached is a partner migration pack that contains:
- A step-by-step migration checklist
- The change matrix (mapping v1 fields to the async API)
- A proposed canary calendar that lines up with Ben's suggestions
- A templated announcement and rollout communications for your customers

Practical asks from our side:
- Confirm you can run the Dockerized test runner in your CI (we included a sample GitHub Actions workflow).
- Confirm a weekly 30-minute sync slot (~Wednesdays 09:00 PDT) starting next week so engineering teams can unblock quickly.
- Confirm whether NimbleWorks wants a white-labeled compatibility shim or prefers to vendor the shim code as open-source under our partner repo.

Also: can we use NimbleWorks' logo and a short customer quote in the migration guide? Marketing would like to feature one early adopter.

Attaching: nimbleworks_bridge-proposal.pdf (partner migration pack)

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Partner Programs — Redwood Inference
[attachment: nimbleworks_bridge-proposal.pdf]
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@nimbleworks.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner migration pack + weekly sync cadence

Thanks everyone — the plan looks good and we appreciate the pragmatic timeline. A few follow-ups before we lock dates: 

- We accept the 6-month soft-deprecation window you proposed, but need explicit canary dates so we can coordinate customer-facing timelines. Can you confirm the proposed start-of-canary date (Ben's Week 1 of rollout)?
- Telemetry: we will want partner-limited access to the dashboard during canary and a daily health digest for the first two weeks. Please confirm retention/PII rules.
- Rollback: please provide a rollback playbook in the migration pack (automated switch-back to v1 behavior if error rates exceed thresholds).

We’ll run the test harness this week and I’ll confirm the Wednesday sync. Attaching our migration plan for your engineers.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the weekly sync.

— Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
Head of Integrations — NimbleWorks
[attachment: nimbleworks_nw_migration_plan.pdf]
